row.category: Vertical SaaS (Healthcare, Education, Real Estate, Construction, Field Service)
row.evidence: Jack Henry sells the Symitar credit-union core platform through sales only, and its public SymXchange developer docs cover member-account transactions and PowerOn specfiles, with no SCIM endpoint or staff-user provisioning.
row.notes: Symitar (Episys) is Jack Henry's credit-union core processing platform, sold on-premises or hosted (Symitar EASE) by quote only; no public plans or prices. Client documentation sits behind Jack Henry's client login, so the public record is thin. Public jackhenry.dev SymXchange docs describe a SOAP web-services API for member accounts (not staff users) and mention an Active Directory feature in the System Web Console, with no detail on staff SSO or provisioning. No SCIM docs, no Okta OIN app (okta.com/integrations/symitar/ 404) and no Entra tutorial found. Left unknown rather than none because client docs could not be searched. See also the jack-henry row.

user_api.notes: SymXchange (SOAP web services) operates on member accounts (transactions, inquiries, file maintenance, PowerOn specfiles); no endpoints for credit-union staff (Episys user) accounts are public.

fallbacks.other_sync: System Web Console lists an Active Directory feature for Symitar; what it syncs or authenticates is not documented publicly
